solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cocktail — doctor and girl consuming it

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a common abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: the girl's name eats up the next word, so it sits inside her

parts.note: Jo is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A medic and his companion share a cocktail, she downing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum, lime and mint drink from Cuba, one well-known example of a cocktail.

definitions.note: the dune grass named here is spelt identically from either end, so the definition is also the whole wordplay

indicators.note: in a down clue pulled up means read bottom to top, and the word stays unaltered that way

parts.note: the dune grass named here is spelt identically from either end, so the definition is also the whole wordplay

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether a weed stays the same when uprooted.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters read the same upwards as downwards, so the clue only needs the definition plus that hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coastal dune grass, an example of grass planted to bind sand.

parts.note: just means only, as in 'just one'
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jeweller praises nothing but diamonds as being of fair quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairness as a virtue or attribute is what justice names, so it is a quality of being fair.

definitions.meaning: sharp or biting, as a remark can be
an open pastry case with a sweet filling

explanation.surface: Someone slicing up a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp remark is tart, and a fruit pastry is a tart: two unrelated senses of one word.

clue.text: Ignoramus retaining job, leader dismissed as cheap

indicators.note: the fool keeps the next piece held within

parts.note: a twit is a foolish person

indicators.note: the first letter of the word job is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before losing its first letter

explanation.surface: A dunce keeps his post after the boss is sacked, and is called cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'job' looks like the dunce's post in the surface, but 'leader dismissed' strips its first letter to leave OB, and 'retaining' sets that inside the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-bit is an American idiom for worthless or shoddy, from a quarter dollar being two bits.

clue.text: Rwanda rebuilt church, as steps taken before battle

indicators.note: rebuilt says the letters of the country are put together in a new order

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: An African country restores a church, with measures taken before fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steps' suggests measures or stairs, but here means dance steps; 'rebuilt' scrambles the country to WARDAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A war dance is a ritual performance of dance steps done to prepare warriors for combat.

definitions.meaning: a metal mixture of copper and zinc

explanation.surface: A metallurgist describing a silver mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is both British slang for cash (as is silver for coins) and a copper–zinc metal blend.

definitions.meaning: hard to put up with, wearing
putting someone on trial in court; the question mark flags the whimsical reading

explanation.surface: A lawyer finds litigation hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoying or hard is trying, and conducting a trial is literally trying a case in court.

parts.note: a celebrity is a star, and a celebrity is someone, a person, who partly shines; the whimsy is that a star twinkles

explanation.surface: Someone gazing at the sky asks whether a star is twinkling a little.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious definition is 'Star' as in a celebrity; the rest plays on stars in the sky twinkling.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous figure in entertainment or public life is commonly called a celebrity or star.

definitions.meaning: to arrange in advance, such as a table
a substitute waiting on the bench in sport

explanation.surface: A team manager sets up a substitute in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To book is to make a booking in advance, and a substitute in a team is a reserve.

clue.text: Prepared to study theology in the end

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word theology

explanation.surface: Someone is set to study divinity eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: Set and prepared for action are synonyms of being all set.

clue.text: Keen to send high-maintenance woman back

indicators.note: together with back, sending something back turns it around, word read backwards
completes the instruction to send the demanding woman backwards

parts.note: a diva is a demanding, temperamental woman

explanation.surface: Someone is eager to get rid of a demanding woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and enthusiastic are synonyms, so keen fits as an adjective.

indicators.note: says the word for a fool is written down two times in succession

parts.note: an ass is a stupid person

explanation.surface: A clown makes two appearances in a murder story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link here but literal letters at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer, especially of a political figure, is an assassin: a killer by trade.

clue.text: Lady, true to form, in act of betrayal

indicators.note: to form says the letters are shaped into something new

explanation.surface: A lady staying faithful amid an act of treachery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to form' rearranges LADY TRUE. The surface's 'true' is ironic against the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital infidelity is a betrayal of one's spouse, so it is an act of betrayal.

parts.note: at a wedding reception the bride and groom slice the tiered confection; reception suggests a hotel desk or hairdresser's

explanation.surface: Someone waiting at a salon front desk for a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reception' and 'cuts' suggest a hairdresser; the reception is a marriage party.
explanation.definitionFit: At a marriage celebration the couple ceremonially make the first slice of the tiered sponge.

clue.text: Ruler about India provided lovely introductions for author

indicators.note: the ruler goes around the following pieces

parts.note: a king is a ruler
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: introductions are the opening letters of the words provided and lovely

explanation.surface: A monarch around India gave lovely introductions for a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling, the writer of The Jungle Book, was an author.

clue.text: Young animal cradling her beautiful infant

indicators.note: cradling means holding in the arms, so the word her sits inside

parts.note: a cub is the young of a bear, fox or lion

explanation.surface: A baby beast hugging a lovely child.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic winged babies in art are cherubs, so a lovely chubby baby is called one.

clue.text: Beginning to sweat, retinue showing evidence of stress

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of sweat

parts.note: a train is a body of attendants following an important person

explanation.surface: An entourage starts to perspire, showing signs of pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension under pressure is strain, which shows visibly when someone is overstretched.

clue.text: House no great thing for island capital

parts.note: a lulu is a remarkable or outstanding example of something

explanation.surface: Swapping a house for nothing remarkable, for an island capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of Hawaii sits on the island of Oahu, so it is an island capital.

explanation.surface: A freshly published volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh and original is novel, and a long prose fiction is a novel.

indicators.note: called back, so the word for hints is turned round

parts.note: tips are hints or clues

explanation.surface: Someone sneers as hints are withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitting at someone is a gesture of scorn, a way to show disdain.

parts.note: to sag is to droop or sink

explanation.surface: A storyteller lets one tale droop on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is an epic narrative, especially a Norse one, hence a lengthy tale.

indicators.note: the university letter breaks into the middle of the next piece
contrary says the word for always is set the opposite way round

parts.note: ever means always, consistently

explanation.surface: A college keeps cutting into a show that is always at odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' turns EVER into REVE, which U enters.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical entertainment of sketches, songs and dances is a revue, a kind of stage show.

indicators.note: out signals the singer's name is put out of order

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra is dropped in favour of a female star.
explanation.definitionFit: The empress of Russia was the woman at the head of the nation, a cryptic sense of leading lady.

clue.text: Noble oddly accepting royalty ultimately in Queen Anne

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the next piece
oddly says the letters of noble are arranged in a strange way
ultimately points to the last letter of the word royalty

explanation.surface: A peer, strangely taking in royalty, becomes a Tudor queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges NOBLE to BOLEN, which 'accepting' wraps round Y. 'oddly' is an anagram signal, not alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Boleyn was Henry VIII's second wife, so she was Queen Anne by marriage.

clue.text: Limit alcoholic drink given to wreck

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A cap on liquor offered to someone in ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge or boundary is a margin, as in a limit of error.
